questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The aspect of experincing central/eastern europe culture and people at these places, and how they practicing academian disciplines. To get a insight of how people gather and study around a former soviet state. Furthermore, it had very intersting and a broad range of subjects to offer.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: More or less easy. There was a lot of information with mail and on Facebook groups, which created a sense of attachment and a space to contact yourself to. Futhermore, responses were very fast and easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved information about introduction to meet people, how to sign up courses and to get around at the destination

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many options were available, but it was not possible to choose the places(residence) to live at. That meant, that I endned up very far from the faculty to go to classes, instead of a more close (and available) residences. So there was a lack of coordination.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Very bad! The kitchen was really non-exsisting. Only two heated hobs to cook and a sink - which you should share with 12 people! The cantine never opened my stay and there was no common rooms to eat or meet.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The lack of common-rooms, the non-existing kitchen and lack of cafées nearby.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A specific date and specific time courses were open to get enrolled in, and it was a mess. A lot of people did not get the courses they had planned to enroll, because courses got filled up very fast and had a maximum amount of space. From that you were on a waiting list, but everyone was not moving away courses because they now had to contact their domestic insitutions for getting courses accepted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not really any,

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very lucky, I got 4 out 5 I had planned to have.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't know. Be lucky. Be on time and be fast on your fingers and have a good internet connection.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Mediocre level. The teachers were competent and enthusiastic, but the abstract level was a bit low.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Smaller classes. Active participation is part of the last grade. More project and group working.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The European Union: Integration and democratization
Introduction to Intellectual History: Approaches and Methods
Religion, secularity and laicity in Europe (19th-21th centuries)
Promoting democracy abroad: the US and the EU in third countries
EU Institutions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Intellectual History: Approaches and Methods
It has a high amount of abstract level, it create a sense of attachment to the fields of academics and its discipline. It has a lot of texts and you get in contact with thinkers work and approaches and its meta-assumptions. You become aware of history and how it is framed, worked out and become a part of intellectual thinking

What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Social activies were avaiable for students through student groups at faculty, through the university as such and through Erasmus institutional programmes. 
Athletic a bit the same
Cultural lacked

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Traveling in the areas around to get to see some more authentic places that are not univserity or service driven. It give a sense of a broader feeling and experince of the country's living standard and how they have a daily life.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to galleries in prague. It is beautiful and have a huge legacy and heritage of aesthic value

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite hard. Not many spoke english and people seemed a bit closed and strange to you. But it helped as you get through months and can speak a few words of the language to create a sense of balance and shared living.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn some few words to get into people in the beginning, from there you have created a safe spot to speak english. Attend to social activites. Do a body-programme.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Western/eastern heritage. Background of history; that western culture is not sacred or holy, but that cultural ideas in eastern has its own value. I experienced a form of shame of eastern europe's heritage and way of living.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Aesthetics and people living a simple life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be flexible; things change and is not easy to grasp from the beginning - have alternatives
Be patient; things take time and it is not easy to get into everything in the beginning - percept it as a process, rather than a result
Have low expectations - things will not be as you thought, which is the best part of it

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: That exchange student is also reading and academics and not just fun

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people with different backgrounds face to face. Their way of living, their dreams and thoughts about things. That is the most rewarding part of life, I believe. Exchange is just a great oppurtunity to experince that and get it much more balanced and safe.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Limiting yourself being part of big community where there is many temptations and ways to go.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
